summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted one day after discharge due to shaking chills and worsening pain around his indwelling urinary catheter site. Initially treated for suspected sepsis with broad-spectrum antibiotics, he was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli and Serratia marcescens. After culture results, antibiotics were narrowed to IV ceftriaxone. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. He also received treatment for bilateral conjunctivitis and facial impetigo. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged to short-term rehab to complete his antibiotic course and address deconditioning. Follow-up was arranged with urology, cardiology, and primary care.
problems: Urinary catheterization as the cause of abnormal reaction
